output.summary: KEP-3136 changes the kube-apiserver so that newly introduced beta APIs are disabled by default, while existing beta APIs and new versions of already-enabled beta APIs stay on by default. Cluster-admins opt in to specific beta resources through an extended --runtime-config flag (group/version/resource=true).
output.rationale: Beta APIs are not considered stable, and defaulting them on exposes most production clusters to bugs and future migration pain. The PRR survey reports over 90% of cluster-admins keep these APIs enabled, so defaulting on puts them in nearly every production cluster. Conformance no longer depends on non-stable APIs, so disabling them by default is now practical.

alternatives.option: Change feature gate defaults so beta features are off by default
alternatives.why_not: The KEP lists this as a non-goal: "Change feature gate defaults. Feature gates control new features (not just new APIs) and they are on by default for beta features."

alternatives.option: Disable all beta APIs, including existing ones and new versions of existing beta APIs
alternatives.why_not: Goal 2 requires continuing to enable existing beta APIs and new versions of existing beta APIs by default, so that v1beta2 of an enabled group stays enabled.

evidence.quote: From the Kubernetes release where this change is introduced, and onwards, beta APIs will not be enabled in clusters by default.
We observed these problems as we removed long-standing beta APIs and the PRR survey tells us that over 90% of cluster-admins leave production clusters with these APIs enabled.
This is now practical to do since conformance no longer relies on non-stable APIs.
New beta APIs will be placed into the `DisableVersions` stanza instead of the `EnableVersions` stanza
To enable a beta API, a cluster-admin will have to add the appropriate `--runtime-config` flags.
